newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun Alliance climbs as sales jump.
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun Alliance climbs as sales jump.

text.p: Shares in Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc rose on Thursday after the company said single premium sales rose more than 113 percent in 1996.
The shares were up 8-1/2p at 470-1/2p by 1004 GMT with more than a million shares traded.
SocGen analyst Charles Landa said on the whole the results were encouraging but he maintains a "hold" rating on the shares.
"The figures were slightly better than expected, driven by the doubling of single premium sales," Landa said. "However the growth in regular premiums at five percent is less exciting."

"Going forward, the company needs to strengthen in the area of personal pensions, and part of this will be to increase the regular premiums," Landa added. "The shares are trading above net asset value," Landa commented. "However, the company is financially strong and is set to produce attractive dividend growth."

The analyst said he expected to see the company start to look for acquisitions in the UK and Continental Europe next year, in preference to making a special dividend in line with some analysts' expectations.
